## 3. Goals (impact map)

### Goal A: Import weekly till sales (vision success criterion 1)
- **Actor:** owner of an independent bookshop (one to three shops) whose till exports weekly sales as CSV.
- **Impact:** every week, the week's sales go into the system instead of sitting unread in an export file.
- **Success metric:** the time from choosing the week's export file to seeing the import confirmation is
  under two minutes. This is measured on the real flow with a real export from the owner's till, and
  includes the owner's own steps.

### Goal B: Monthly report and reorder list (vision success criterion 2)
- **Actor:** the same owner.
- **Impact:** the owner reorders from a report of what actually sold instead of from memory. Bestsellers
  get restocked and slow sellers do not get reordered.
- **Success metric:** the time from opening the month's report to holding a finished reorder list
  (downloaded or printed) is under ten minutes. This is measured on the real flow with a real month of
  imported sales.

| 2 | `plans/functional/bookshop-sales-insights-monthly-report-and-reorder-list.md` | Calendar-month bestseller and slow-seller report built from imported sales (all shops or one shop, missing weeks flagged); reorder list that starts with the bestsellers; edit it; add any title; download or print it; keep each month's list | 8 | 3 | 1 |

- Level 1 (needs only A1.1): A1.2, A1.3, A2.1, A3.1, B1.1, B2.1

## 7. Decisions taken under ambiguity (full list)

1. **Two goals, two stubs, not one plan.** Criterion 1 (import) and criterion 2 (report and reorder)
   have the same actor but different impacts, so impact mapping gives two goals. The report is built
   only from imported sales, so the report stub depends on the import stub. My method treats a
   cross-goal dependency as a reason to consider merging. Merging would give one plan of 15 stories,
   which goes back to the Vision Advisor as a single-plan conversion. I kept two because each goal has
   its own measurable criterion and can be accepted on its own, and the dependency runs one way (import
   never needs the report). Splitting by goal, rather than into a "walking skeleton stub" plus "the
   rest", also leaves the build order with the owner. The one-plan alternative is open for the owner.
2. **The reorder list is not a third goal.** Criterion 2 measures the report and the reorder together
   ("reorders from it in under ten minutes"). Same actor and same impact, so they merge into one goal.
3. **Till export layout is assumed, because the vision does not give one.** Assumed layout: a header
   row, then columns for sale date, product code, title and quantity sold. A shop column is used if
   present and other columns are ignored. The separator is a comma or a semicolon, and the encoding is
   UTF-8 (with or without a byte-order mark) or Windows-1252. A1.2 (match the columns once) handles a
   different layout. The owner is asked for one real export.
4. **An item is identified by the till's product code.** For books that is the ISBN/EAN. The title is
   only for display. A row without a product code counts as an unreadable line. Non-book items the till
   sells (cards, gifts) are imported and reported like books, and the owner is asked whether to keep
   them out.
5. **Returns:** a negative quantity is a return. It is stored and counts against that product code's
   copies sold, so the report shows net copies.
6. **Weeks and months:** each sale keeps its own date. The report uses calendar months by sale date, so
   a week from 30 March to 5 April counts its March days in March and its April days in April. An
   imported week is shown as the date range of its file's rows.
7. **Duplicate import:** an import is a duplicate if it contains sale dates already imported for the
   same shop. The owner is warned with the dates, shop and earlier row count, and chooses to replace
   those dates' sales or cancel.
8. **Bestsellers:** the 20 titles with the most net copies sold in the month, highest first, ties
   ordered by title. Ranked by copies, not revenue, because the reorder is in copies and the vision sets
   no revenue goal.
9. **Slow sellers: the main ambiguity.** Only sales are imported, so a title that sold nothing has no
   rows and cannot be seen. Rule: a slow seller is a title that sold at least once in the three calendar
   months before the report month and sold 0 or 1 net copies in the report month, fewest first. A title
   that never sold, or has not sold for more than three months, cannot be shown without stock data, and
   the vision does not import stock. The owner is asked.
10. **Missing-week warning:** the report warns when a whole Monday–Sunday week inside the month (or the
    part of that week that falls inside the month) has no sales for the selected shop or shops. A single
    day without sales does not trigger the warning, because shops close on some days. A shop closed for
    a whole week (a holiday) will set off the warning. This is acceptable because it only warns and
    never blocks.
11. **Suggested reorder quantity** = net copies sold in the month ("replace what sold"). The owner edits it.
12. **The report and the reorder list share the bestseller and slow-seller rules, and neither needs the
    other.** Whichever of B1.1 and B2.1 is built first implements the rules and the other reuses them.
    B2.1 can be opened from the report when the report exists, and directly for a chosen month
    otherwise. This keeps every chain at three stories. Otherwise "change quantities" would need the
    list, the list would need the report, and the report would need the import: four deep.
13. **Shops:** an owner with one shop never sees a shop choice. Owners with two or three shops tag each
    import with a shop, picked from the shops they have named or named new, or taken from a shop column
    if the export has one. The report shows all shops together or one shop. A reorder list started from
    the report follows the report's shop selection.
14. **The reorder list ends in a CSV download and a printout.** Ordering from suppliers is out of the
    vision's own scope.
15. **Platform, hosting and accounts are not in the vision.** The stubs stay solution-neutral.
    Implementation planning needs an answer: a local tool for one owner, or a hosted service with
    logins? The sales figures are the owner's business data.
16. **Measuring the time targets:** the 2-minute and 10-minute targets are measured on the real human
    flow (file chosen → confirmation shown; report opened → list downloaded or printed), not in unit
    tests. A weekly export is assumed to have at most 10,000 rows. This assumption is not verified, and
    the owner's real export will settle it.
17. **Returns are part of A1.1, not a story of their own.** On its own the story would be well under two
    hours of work.
18. **The slow-seller warning on the reorder list is part of B2.3 (add any title), not a story of its
    own.** A slow seller only gets onto the list when it is added by hand, so a separate story would have
    needed B2.3 and sat four deep.
19. **No release phases.** My method normally groups the remaining stories into "flesh out" and
    "polish" phases. I did not do that: the owner alone decides what is built and when. `[MVP]` only
    marks structure (membership of the walking skeleton). The dependency levels above say what must
    exist first and nothing more.
20. **Foundation dependencies are kept:** A1.2 and A1.3 depend on A1.1, and B2.2 and B2.3 depend on
    B2.1, within the same activity. Merging each into its foundation would make that story larger than
    three days, so they stay separate. Each depends on the foundation only.
21. **Interactive questions were not asked.** This is a background run. The goal-validation question
    and the delivery-strategy question are listed in section 8 for the owner. The delivery-strategy
    question is the owner's scheduling call and I have not answered it.
22. **`dependsOn` slug form:** I pass `import-weekly-till-sales` (the goal slug), following the
    documented example `dependsOn: ["goal-1-slug"]`. I could not check the library to see whether it
    expects the full stub slug `bookshop-sales-insights-import-weekly-till-sales`. The session should
    check before running.
23. **Where this draft lives:** under `.ctoc/decomposition/`, so that it is not mistaken for a stub in
    `plans/functional/` or a vision in `plans/vision/`. Stubs are only ever created by the library.

## 8. Decisions waiting for the owner's review

1. **Goals:** two goals (import weekly till sales; monthly report and reorder list) as two stubs, with
   the report stub depending on the import stub. Or one plan through the Vision Advisor?
2. **Till export:** which till is it? Please supply one real weekly export (anonymised is fine) to
   confirm or correct the assumed layout (decision 3) and the 10,000-row ceiling (decision 16).
3. **Slow sellers:** accept the rule (sold at least once in the previous three months, 0–1 copies this
   month)? Or bring in stock levels so that titles that never sold become visible? Stock import would
   change the vision's scope, so it is your call.
4. **Bestsellers:** 20 titles ranked by copies sold, or a different number, or ranked by revenue?
5. **Suggested reorder quantity:** copies sold that month, or another rule?
6. **Non-book items** (cards, gifts) on the report: included as the till sells them, or kept out?
7. **Hosting and access:** a local tool for one owner, or hosted with logins?
8. **Delivery strategy and build order:** which stories to build, and when. Section 5 gives only what
   must exist first.

1. Run `validateVisionReadiness` from `src/lib/vision-decomposer.js` on
   `plans/vision/bookshop-sales-insights.md` (check its argument form in the source first).

Traces to vision success criterion 1.', dependsOn:[]},

Each month list is kept. Traces to vision success criterion 2.', dependsOn:['import-weekly-till-sales']}
   ```bash
   ]); console.log(JSON.stringify(r,null,2))"
   ```

3. Re-dispatch vision-decomposer to add each insert block below to its stub with `Edit`. The
   `old_string` is the stub's `## Scope` heading line. The `new_string` is the block followed by that
   same `## Scope` line. Never `Write` over a stub.
4. Show the owner the stub table (section 4) and the decisions waiting for review (section 8), with the
   checkpoint question ("Looks good, refine all" / "Edit stubs" / "Add a stub" / "Start over").
   **Stop there and wait for the owner's OK.**
5. Only after the owner's OK: `writeStatus` (`src/lib/background.js`) per stub,
   `initBackgroundAgent(AGENT_TYPES.PRODUCT_OWNER, …)` (`src/lib/actions.js`) per stub, then
   `completeVision` (`src/lib/vision-decomposer.js`).

## Decomposition

Parent vision: `plans/vision/bookshop-sales-insights.md`, success criterion 1 ("An owner imports a week
of till sales from the CSV export in under two minutes"). Decomposed by vision-decomposer on
2026-10-06. No canvas exists for this vision.

### Goal: An owner imports a week of till sales from the CSV export in under two minutes
- **Actor:** owner of an independent bookshop (one to three shops) whose till exports weekly sales as CSV.
- **Impact:** every week, the week's sales go into the system instead of sitting unread in an export file.
- **Success metric:** the time from choosing the week's export file to seeing the import confirmation is
  under two minutes. This is measured on the real flow with a real export from the owner's till, and
  includes the owner's own steps.

### Activities (backbone, in the order the owner does them)
1. Bring in the week's export
2. Deal with problems in the export
3. Check which weeks are in

`[MVP]` marks a walking-skeleton story: the simplest story in its activity. Together these stories form
the thinnest end-to-end path. The marker records structure only. Which stories are built, and when, is
the owner's decision.

### Activity 1: Bring in the week's export

**Walking skeleton:**
- [ ] [MVP] **A1.1:** As an owner, I want to choose my till's weekly CSV export and have its sales
  stored, so that the week's sales are ready for my monthly report instead of sitting unread in a file.
  - Acceptance:
    - Given an export with a header row and columns for sale date, product code, title and quantity, and
      312 data rows dated 2–8 March 2026: choosing it stores all 312 rows, and the owner sees
      "312 sales rows imported, N titles, 2–8 March 2026".
    - Comma-separated and semicolon-separated files are both read. UTF-8 (with or without a byte-order
      mark) and Windows-1252 files both keep accented titles intact (e.g. "Één dag in Gent").
    - A row with a negative quantity is stored as a return and counts against that product code: rows
      +5 and −1 for the same ISBN give 4 net copies. The confirmation shows the number of return rows.
    - A 10,000-row export goes from file chosen to confirmation shown in under two minutes, including
      the owner's steps, measured on the real flow.
    - Each stored sale keeps its sale date, product code, title, quantity and source file name.
  - Depends on: nothing. This is the foundation: it sets up the sales storage that every other story,
    in both stubs, reads.

**Additional stories:**
- [ ] **A1.2:** As an owner whose till names or orders its columns differently, I want to tell the
  import once which column holds the sale date, product code, title and quantity, so that my till's
  export imports, and later weeks import without asking again.
  - Acceptance:
    - Given an export with headers `Datum;EAN;Omschrijving;Aantal`, the owner is asked once to match
      them to sale date / product code / title / quantity. After confirming, the rows import as in A1.1.
    - The next export with the same headers imports with no matching step.
    - An export with different headers asks again and starts from the previous match.
    - Dates written day-first (`09-03-2026`) are read as 9 March 2026 once the owner has confirmed the
      date order.
  - Depends on: A1.1.
- [ ] **A1.3:** As an owner of two or three shops, I want each import to record which shop it came from,
  so that my report can show each shop's sales separately as well as together.
  - Acceptance:
    - The owner picks the shop from the shops they have named, or names a new one (e.g. "Centrum",
      "Noord"). If the export has a shop column, the shop is taken from it. The confirmation names the
      shop.
    - An owner who has named only one shop is never asked to pick one.
    - Sales for Centrum and Noord in the same week are both kept, and neither replaces the other.
    - Where imported weeks are listed (A3.1), each entry names its shop.
  - Depends on: A1.1.

### Activity 2: Deal with problems in the export

**Walking skeleton:**
- [ ] [MVP] **A2.1:** As an owner, I want lines that cannot be read listed with their line number and
  reason while the rest of the week imports, and a file that is not a sales export refused with a plain
  message, so that one bad line never blocks my week and I know when I picked the wrong file.
  - Acceptance:
    - Given a 100-row export where line 17 has quantity `abc` and line 42 has no date: 98 rows are
      imported, and the owner sees "Line 17: quantity 'abc' is not a number" and "Line 42: no sale date".
    - A row without a product code is listed the same way and is not stored.
    - Choosing a PDF, an empty file, or a CSV with no recognisable sales columns imports nothing and
      says which of these it was.
  - Depends on: A1.1.

**Additional stories:**
- [ ] **A2.2:** As an owner, I want to be warned when I import sales for dates I already imported for
  the same shop, and choose to replace them or cancel, so that no sale is counted twice in my report.
  - Acceptance:
    - Importing the 2–8 March export for Centrum a second time shows "2–8 March for Centrum is already
      imported (312 rows)". Replace: those dates hold exactly the new file's rows. Cancel: nothing changes.
    - An export for 5–11 March, when 2–8 March is already in, warns naming 5–8 March. Replace swaps only
      those dates' rows.
    - The same week for a different shop imports without a warning.
  - Depends on: A1.1, A1.3.

### Activity 3: Check which weeks are in

**Walking skeleton:**
- [ ] [MVP] **A3.1:** As an owner, I want to see every week I have imported with its row count and
  import date, so that I can confirm the weeks I expect are in before I rely on the report.
  - Acceptance:
    - After importing 2–8 March and 9–15 March, the list shows both, newest first, each with its date
      range, number of rows and the date it was imported.
    - With no imports yet, the list says "No weeks imported yet" and explains how to import.
  - Depends on: A1.1.

**Additional stories:**
- [ ] **A3.2:** As an owner, I want to remove a week I imported, so that I can undo importing the wrong
  file.
  - Acceptance:
    - Removing 9–15 March asks for confirmation naming the dates and the row count. After confirming,
      those rows are gone from storage and from every report, and the list no longer shows that week.
    - Other weeks are untouched.
  - Depends on: A3.1.

### Story dependencies (technical, not a build order)
- A1.1: nothing
- A1.2, A1.3, A2.1, A3.1: A1.1
- A2.2: A1.1, A1.3
- A3.2: A3.1
- Longest chain: 3 (A2.2 → A1.3 → A1.1; A3.2 → A3.1 → A1.1). No cycles.

### Dependency on other stubs
None. Stub `bookshop-sales-insights-monthly-report-and-reorder-list` depends on this stub: every report
and reorder story needs A1.1 (stored sales), and the per-shop report needs A1.3 (shop recorded).

## Decisions Taken Under Ambiguity
1. **Two stubs, not one plan.** Import (criterion 1) and report-and-reorder (criterion 2) share an actor
   but have different impacts. The report depends on this stub, one way only. The one-plan alternative
   is open for the owner.
2. **Assumed till export layout** (the vision gives none): a header row; sale date, product code, title
   and quantity columns; a shop column used if present; comma or semicolon separator; UTF-8 or
   Windows-1252. A1.2 handles other layouts. Waiting on a real export from the owner.
3. **Item identity** is the till's product code (the ISBN/EAN for books). The title is for display only.
   A row without a code is an unreadable line. Non-book items are imported like books, pending the
   owner's answer.
4. **Returns** (negative quantities) are part of A1.1 and count against sales. On their own they would
   be well under two hours of work.
5. **Dates:** each sale keeps its own date. An imported week is the date range of its file's rows.
   A duplicate means dates already imported for the same shop.

## Decomposition

Parent vision: `plans/vision/bookshop-sales-insights.md`, success criterion 2 ("An owner opens a monthly
report of bestsellers and slow sellers, built from the sales they imported, and reorders from it in
under ten minutes"). Decomposed by vision-decomposer on 2026-10-06. No canvas exists for this vision.

### Goal: An owner reorders from a monthly bestseller and slow-seller report in under ten minutes
- **Actor:** owner of an independent bookshop (one to three shops).
- **Impact:** the owner reorders from a report of what actually sold instead of from memory. Bestsellers
  get restocked and slow sellers do not get reordered.
- **Success metric:** the time from opening the month's report to holding a finished reorder list
  (downloaded or printed) is under ten minutes. This is measured on the real flow with a real month of
  imported sales.

### Activities (backbone, in the order the owner does them)
1. Read the month's report
2. Build the reorder list
3. Use the reorder list

`[MVP]` marks a walking-skeleton story: the simplest story in its activity. Together these stories form
the thinnest end-to-end path. The marker records structure only. Which stories are built, and when, is
the owner's decision.

### Activity 1: Read the month's report

**Walking skeleton:**
- [ ] [MVP] **B1.1:** As an owner, I want to open a report for a calendar month listing my bestsellers
  and my slow sellers from the sales I imported, so that I see what to restock and what not to reorder
  without going through the weekly files.
  - Acceptance:
    - Given imported sales where in March 2026 "Title X" sold 40 net copies and "Title Y" sold 1, and
      Title Y also sold 6 in January 2026: the March report lists Title X among the bestsellers with 40,
      and Title Y among the slow sellers with "1 sold in March".
    - Bestsellers are the 20 titles with the most net copies sold in the month, highest first, ties
      ordered by title.
    - Slow sellers are titles that sold at least once in the three calendar months before the chosen
      month and sold 0 or 1 net copies in it, fewest first.
    - Sales count in the month of their sale date: a week from 30 March to 5 April adds its March days
      to March and its April days to April.
    - A month with no imported sales shows "No sales imported for March 2026", not an empty table.
  - Depends on: A1.1 "Choose the export and store its sales" (stub

## Decisions Taken Under Ambiguity
1. **Two stubs, not one plan.** This stub depends on the import stub, one way only. The one-plan
   alternative is open for the owner.
2. **The reorder list belongs to this goal, not a goal of its own.** Criterion 2 measures report and
   reorder together.

   copies, not revenue (the reorder is in copies, and the vision sets no revenue goal and allows only
   one currency).
4. **Slow sellers:** only sales are imported, so a title that sold nothing is invisible. Rule: sold at
   least once in the three calendar months before the report month, and 0 or 1 net copies in it.
   Titles that never sold, or have not sold for more than three months, cannot be shown without stock
   data, which the vision does not import. Waiting on the owner.
5. **Months** are calendar months by sale date. A week that crosses a month boundary is split.
6. **Missing-week warning:** a whole Monday–Sunday week (or the part of it inside the month) with no
   sales triggers it, single days do not. A shop closed for a holiday week triggers it too. This is
   accepted because it only warns.
7. **Suggested reorder quantity** = net copies sold that month. Waiting on the owner.
8. **The report and the reorder list share the ranking rules, and neither story needs the other.** This
   keeps every chain at three stories or fewer.
9. **The slow-seller warning is part of B2.3**, because a slow seller only reaches the list when added
   by hand.
10. **Shops:** the report shows all shops together or one shop. A list started from the report follows
    its selection. An owner with one shop sees no switch.
